1A.title: Rehberli Alıştırma 1: Ana Fikir Tespiti (SCOPE)
1A.passage: For centuries, European cartographers depicted the interior of the African continent as an empty void or filled it with mythical beasts, reflecting European ignorance rather than African reality. In truth, complex trade networks, vibrant kingdoms such as Mali and Great Zimbabwe, and sophisticated urban centers flourished long before European exploration. Recent archaeological findings and translations of Arabic and local manuscripts have increasingly forced modern historians to abandon Eurocentric narratives and recognize Africa's dynamic precolonial history.

choices.A: European cartographers frequently decorated maps with illustrations of mythical creatures.
choices.B: Historical evidence is replacing inaccurate European depictions of precolonial Africa with a richer understanding of its advanced societies.
choices.C: Translations of Arabic manuscripts represent the single most important development in African historical research.
choices.D: The kingdoms of Mali and Great Zimbabwe maintained trade networks across the African continent.

1A.passage: Bioluminescence—the production of light by living organisms—serves diverse ecological functions in marine environments. While terrestrial bioluminescence is relatively rare, over 75% of deep-sea creatures possess this capability. Predators like the anglerfish use glowing lures to attract prey, while smaller organisms like dinoflagellates emit flashes of light to startle predators or signal larger hunters to attack their pursuers. Far from being a mere decorative novelty, bioluminescence is a critical survival mechanism in the sunless depths.

1A.passage: In 1938, Dutch painter Han van Meegeren forged several paintings attributed to the seventeenth-century master Johannes Vermeer, deceiving renowned art historians and earning millions. When van Meegeren was later tried for selling Dutch national treasures, he had to paint a new forgery in his jail cell to convince skeptical judges that the works were indeed his own creations.

choices.B: He painted in front of skeptical judges while held in a Dutch detention facility.

choices.D: He forged certificates of authenticity from Vermeer's descendants.

1B.passage: Ecologist Dr. Elena Rostova hypothesized that urban noise pollution impairs songbird breeding success not by directly stressing adult birds, but by masking mating calls, which prevents females from locating prospective mates in high-traffic territories.
